Rate the finding: `real` (a real defect at head), `style`, `wrong`, or `not-a-finding`.

## Finding

``` text
head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:494 — The direct-API (`auth_type: http_api`) `claude-opus-5-5` entry's input bound goes from 180,000 to 936,000, based on one measurement taken through a different route: the claude-headless CLI on Bedrock. The tool's own outcome for that run was `partial` (the budget cap stopped it), and its contract (`--write-catalog` only on `clean`) would have refused to write this. The 180K cap was set by probing cheval's own streaming HTTP transport, and nothing here measures that transport at 936K. The entry is now marked calibrated (`operator_set` + `calibrated_at`), so observed context-limit verdicts never lower it (LSP-5's calibrated branch). Every direct-API host and downstream mount will therefore send up to 936K per call with no self-correction. Scope the value to the measured route, or keep 180K on the HTTP entry until the API-transport probe named in `reprobe_trigger` has run.
head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:504 — `source: operator_set` together with `method: probed_headless` and a `measured_input_tokens` field makes a hand-written value from a `partial` probe look like a tool-written clean calibration. The schema and readers (`_measured()` in the floor test, loa-status "calibrated", routing input_bound) cannot tell the two apart. Record the `partial` outcome (or leave out `method`/`measured_input_tokens`) so provenance stays honest.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:125 — With the opt-in off, chev …
```
